tspan.tspan: A histogram-based method to extract tag-image

text.tspan: Benjamin SERVA1, William PUECH1, Frédéric COMBY1,
1LIRMM, Univ Montpellier, CNRS (France), 2RIRRA21, Université de Montpellier Paul-Valéry (France)
Film analysis begins with shot segmentation, performed either manually by experts
or automatically using shot boundary detection methods [1].
A feature film: tens to hundreds of shots.
An object detector represents each frame as an
objects located near the center of the frame over
according to their temporal position within the
Keyframe: A set of frames representing key stages of a motion or action.
Tag-Image: A single frame representing the overall content of one shot.
Associate each shot with a single representative image (tag-image) that best
identifies the shot and its temporal position within the narrative.
Comparison of results obtained for the shot taken
from the film “Le dîner de cons” [2].
We compare our approach with four representative tag-image selection methods:
Middle Frame: naïve baseline selecting the central frame of the shot.
Pei et al. [3]: optical flow + HSV histogram based selection.
Zhang et al. [4]: multi-feature fusion using color, structure and motion.
Chen et al. [5]: object detection with image quality guided selection.
Our method more consistently selects the
